name: Babylonian glazed brick
summary: Moulded bricks of fired clay that Neo-Babylonian builders glazed in blue, yellow and white. They set the bricks into walls of lions, bulls and dragons on the gates and the Processional Way of Babylon.

philosophy.core_thesis: A mud-brick city wall becomes a royal image when each brick is moulded, glazed blue and fired, so that the animals of the gods stand in a row along the road.
design_principles: Mould each brick as one part of a relief, and number the bricks on the side for the builders.
Glaze the visible face in a vivid blue, and keep the figures in white, yellow and black.
Set the animals in a rhythm: a lion, a bull or a dragon every 1 to 2 m along the wall.
Frame a field of figures with bands of rosettes and a plain blue ground.
Lay the bricks in courses, so that the joints of the wall run along the lines of the relief.
Fire a moulded brick once more after the glaze; a thin bitumen mortar binds the courses.
Face the walls of gates and processional streets only: the ordinary city stays in plain brick.
anti_patterns: A smooth, flat wall of one colour with no moulded figures
A single large slab in place of numbered bricks
Pale, translucent glaze with no deep blue
Figures that fill the whole wall with no blue ground
A body of white porcelain or fine stoneware

form.shape: Rectangular glazed bricks that make up walls, gate towers and wall friezes. Each brick carries part of a moulded animal or a rosette band.
form.profile: A flat wall face with low relief; the figures stand 2 to 4 cm proud of the ground and the gate towers step back in rectangular recesses.
form.foot_and_rim: A brick has no foot. The edges are square and sharp so that the courses fit; the top of the wall ends in a stepped crown of glazed brick.
form.proportion: A brick is about 30 to 35 cm long and 10 to 12 cm thick; the Ishtar Gate rose to about 14 m and the animals measure about 1 m long.
rules: Mould the relief in sections that match the brick size.
Keep the ground a flat, deep blue.
Repeat one animal along the wall in strict rows.
Put the border of rosettes above and below the animals.

bodies.rule: Press a coarse, sandy brick clay into wooden moulds and dry it; the glaze needs a porous, rough body. Keep fine white bodies out of the wall.

methods: pressing clay into wooden relief moulds
cutting the brick to the grid
numbering the bricks on the side
forming.joins: The bricks are laid in courses with bitumen as the mortar, so that each brick sits in the place that the number gives.
forming.details: A number or a mark on the side of a brick, a slightly uneven glaze edge, and a thin dark line of glaze between the figures.

glaze.pattern: Blue ground with white and yellow lions, golden bulls and snake-dragons in rows, and bands of white and yellow rosettes at the top and bottom.
glaze.gloss: Glassy and bright, about 70 to 90 GU; the blue glaze is thick and the colour deepens where it pools in the relief.
glaze.wear: The glaze flakes from the edges of the brick and shows the sandy body; the blue stays strong and the white turns cream.

palette.strategy: A deep lapis-blue ground with warm white and yellow figures; the colour in the glaze comes from copper, cobalt and antimony.

firing.kiln: A large updraught brick kiln with wood and reed fuel; the glazed bricks sit in rows with space round each piece.
processes: moulding and drying of the bricks
a first firing of the brick body
painting of the glaze in colour fields
a second firing of the glaze at about 950 °C
firing.scale: About 15 m of wall for each gate tower; the Ishtar Gate and the Processional Way used many thousands of bricks.
firing.signs: A numbered brick side, a wall of repeated animals, and a blue glaze that ran a little over the edge of the relief.

lineage.root: This is the earliest architectural ceramic style in the data, so no older style of the data leads to it.

emotion.target_response: Awe and order: the viewer walks along a wall where a blue ground and a line of beasts show the power of the king and the gods.

use_cases: a museum label or a reconstruction image of the Ishtar Gate
a gate or wall design with a repeated animal frieze
a prompt for an ancient city in glazed blue brick

the brief needs a hand-painted scene
the brief asks for a matt, earth-coloured wall

modifiers.request: Chinese palace roof, yellow and green
modifiers.how: Change the brick to a roof tile, use a lead glaze in yellow and green, and move the relief to the ridge.

modifiers.request: modern cladding with a baked clay face
modifiers.how: Change to hollow terracotta panels with a matt face, hung on a rail with an air gap.

wall_thickness.note: A whole brick is about 100 mm thick; the knob counts the glazed face layer up to its top of 40 mm.
